decision.latencyConclusion: No full-flow speedup demonstrated: median registration-to-verified-signature 9950.293 ms baseline and 9979.612 ms candidate. Keep the verified request reduction; do not attribute unchanged Yao or finalization paths to this patch.

setupPersistence.scope: D1 API calls for the two setup records only; counted from the exercised code path, not a hosted total-D1 measurement

method: Three fresh implicit, unfunded NEAR wallets per sequential baseline and candidate arm. Corrected NEP-413 SDK, Runtime, Console, Router, Deriver A/B, Signing Worker, configuration and requested APAC placement stayed fixed. Only the four Gateway bundles changed. All local checks and builds completed before timing. There is no restored-baseline measurement arm. The first three baseline samples lacked Console observation and remain in initialInstrumentationAttempt; the baseline was repeated once with all six streams before candidate deployment.

limitations: Invocation wall time includes background work after the HTTP response.
Event timestamp differences include transit, scheduling, execution, and possible clock skew. They do not isolate network latency.

initialInstrumentationAttempt.cause: Console tail produced no events; other five roles captured matching serving versions. Console stream restarted once.

independentSignatureVerification.verifier: Node.js crypto Ed25519 with independent NEP-413 Borsh encoding

limitations: Three samples per arm do not establish percentiles, statistical significance or a latency guarantee.
Sequential arms are exposed to provider scheduling and network variation.
All captured serving versions must match the expected cohort. No failed or mismatched sample is excluded.
Fresh wallets do not prove cold Workers. Worker cold starts were not controlled.
Nested spans overlap. Protocol spans include transport and are not pure CPU measurements.
The two-arm comparison cannot separate small end-to-end differences from provider and network variation.
Worker clocks do not advance during synchronous CPU work. Zero spans do not imply zero work.
Bound-root D1 counters cover admission and execution, not all D1 work in the full flow.
Requested APAC placement does not prove physical colocation.
